## 316630: all-parameter proof, exactly Haase's public theorem
Let I be the H-orbit partition and K its setwise stabilizer in G. H is contained in K and the K-orbits equal the H-orbits. For any finite permutation group J, its average permutation matrix has entry 1/|J.i| if i,j lie in the same orbit, and zero otherwise: the set sending j to i is a stabilizer coset. Thus the averages of H and K coincide, say A. If P(H) is the face maximizing a functional f with value c, then f(A)=c. Since every k in K is in G, f(k)<=c. Their average equals c, forcing equality for every k. Hence k belongs to P(H). A permutation matrix in a convex combination of other permutation matrices must equal each constituent of positive weight: at its zero entries all constituents have zero entries, and its unique one in each row determines the constituent. Therefore K is contained in H. This includes H=G, the trivial subgroup, and the empty ground-set group; averages are nonempty because every subgroup contains the identity.

Alternative geometric route: partition-preserving permutations are exactly vertices supported on the union of orbit squares; minimizing the sum of entries outside these squares exposes P(K). The common group barycenter lies in the relative interiors of both faces, so they are equal. Merely knowing a support face contains P(H) is insufficient without the barycenter step. Both routes are fully paid ordinary finite arguments.

## 382558: arbitrary-crosscut nerve route, precise unclosed bridge
Actual Kozlov0503613 source Section5 definitions, Theorem5.2 and proof, general-crosscut construction, Conjectures5.6–5.7 read. Its theorem explicitly uses a finite lattice. C is an antichain in the proper part and any chain can be extended by a C element. A subset S of C is a crosscut simplex iff join(S)<1 or meet(S)>0. The atom-only theorem is insufficient for arbitrary C. The source expressly warns that the suggested direct collapse to the meet/join subposet can fail.

Let K=Delta(proper L). For c in C let K_c be chains all of whose elements are comparable with c. This covers every simplex by crosscut saturation. K_c is a cone with apex c. For |S|>=2, an element comparable with every member of S must lie below them all or above them all: lying between two incomparable C elements is impossible. Thus intersection K_c over S is the order complex of lower common bounds followed by upper common bounds. If meet(S)>0, that meet is a cone vertex comparable to every such bound. If join(S)<1 the join likewise gives a cone. If neither holds there is no vertex. Singleton intersections are cones too. Therefore the cover nerve is exactly Gamma(C,L), and every nonempty intersection is collapsible, not merely contractible.
